title: Declarative rollback journal + safety-probe for automated canaries and shadowed traffic
author: Evan Park
description: Motivation: Production rollouts have complex failure modes when multi-metric canaries and shadow traffic are used together. Existing controllers could either silently swap traffic back or require manual intervention. This PR introduces a declarative rollback journal and a lightweight safety-probe that records deterministic rollback rationale and enables automated, auditable rollback/replay decisions across canary/A-B/shadow strategies. Design summary: 1) Rollback journal: an append-only, per-rollout record saved in the control plane that stores snapshoted metric windows, decision traces (why a checkpoint failed), and the set of fallback actions taken. Journal entries are immutable and include a deterministic decision-id so downstream automation (alerts, incident tooling) can correlate events. 2) Safety-probe: a small runtime agent that performs low-cost synthetic checks (probe sequences) against candidate model variants using the same routing and KV-cache behavior as production, and reports pass/fail with confidence scores to the rollout controller. 3) Declarative API: new fields on the Rollout CRD (rollbackJournal.enabled, rollbackJournal.retentionDays, safetyProbe.profile, safetyProbe.syntheticRequestsPerMinute) allow operators to opt-in and tune behavior. 4) Compatibility: default behaviour is opt-in; existing rollout flows remain unchanged unless the CR toggles the journal or probe. 5) Failure modes & remediation: journal entries include canonical rollback reasons (latency spike, perplexity regression, toxicity alert) and a suggested remedial action (pause, scale-up, pin-old-model). Implementation highlights: the controller writes journal entries via the existing control plane WAL subsystem and signals a short-lived rollout annotation when a journal entry is created. The safety-probe reuses the serving runtime's routing shim to produce realistic traffic shapes; probes are rate-limited and isolated to avoid perturbing production caches. Testing: added unit, integration, and e2e tests (rollout replay, journal replay, safety-probe edge cases). Rollout plan: staged rollouts across internal clusters for 48h with metric gates and canary percentages, then gradual opt-in for customers using Dedicated. Backwards compatibility: CRD changes are additive; default-off ensures safe upgrade. Open questions: retention policy defaults, and how the journal is surfaced in Console (followup UI PR planned). Related: ENG-1184 (safety automation) and SUP-332 (customer incident that motivated the journal).

release_notes: Added an opt-in rollback journal and safety-probe for rollout controllers. Operators can enable declarative journaling to capture auditable rollback decisions and enable automated safe rollbacks. Safety-probe provides synthetic, low-impact checks for candidate models to reduce false positives during canaries. Default is opt-in; see docs/rollouts/rollback-journal.md for operation and runbook.
notes_for_oncall: If customers report unexpected rollbacks after upgrade, check rollout annotations for journal entries and examine the safety-probe logs. Journal retention defaults to 30 days; retention config is available on the Rollout CRD. If probe traffic affects cache hit rate, toggle safetyProbe.cacheIsolation to true and reopen a followup PR to tune the profile.
